assertion.rationale: CORRECTION (Task 23 register reconciliation): the #f10 evidence anchor and F10's rationale sentence were both dropped from this file by commit 7589a11 (the same commit that closed F10) and never restored, so this record silently stopped mentioning a control contributor that the findings-index table (compliance/findings/2026-08-26-prepublication-review.md) still lists against 3.1.5 to this day. Restored here rather than left stale — the same defect shape (a record no longer matching the table it derives from) this branch exists to eliminate, just by omission instead of by a false claim. F10: the NIST policy identity held standing subscription-scoped Contributor it could never exercise, because the initiative's enforcementMode is DoNotEnforce, so no remediation ever runs and the grant was pure unused risk, surviving RG-scoped teardown because the assignment lives at subscription scope. F10 is now CLOSED (Task 11, commit 7589a11): infra/bicep/landing-zone/main.bicep's NIST initiative assignment sets roleDefinitionIds: [] — the identity is still created and the assignment still validates (ARM requires an identity when an initiative contains deployIfNotExists/modify members; it does not require any role assignment), but it no longer holds a grant it cannot use. F13: privilege across the estate is inverted — Owner and ReadWrite.All exist where automation is fully automated, while seven documented least-privilege workload grants (data-api, mcp-tools, cost-ingest) exist nowhere in code. F7 and F8, this control's other two contributors, are now CLOSED (Task 9, commit 5527354, and Task 10, commit f4c975c, respectively): mls-verifier is federated to its own environment:verify subject distinct from the deployer's (closing F7 — see 3.1.6/3.1.7), and the deployer's Graph grant is Application.ReadWrite.OwnedBy rather than .All (closing F8). Task 12 expresses five of F13's seven grants in least-privilege form: data-api and mcp-tools each get Log Analytics Reader and Security Reader scoped no wider than the role permits (LAW resource scope and subscription scope respectively — neither role has a narrower resource to bind to), mcp-tools gets Cost Management Reader, and data-api's SQL contained-database user and Fabric workspace Viewer grants are expressed via data/seed/sql/900-contained-users.sql and a new Add-FabricWorkspaceRoleAssignment function in infra/fabric/fabric-api.psm1. Task 17 (F15, now CLOSED) lands the sixth in least-privilege form too: the cost export's identity is workflow-created, not Bicep-created, because `az costmanagement export create`/`update` has no --identity-type flag and its pinned API version (2020-06-01) hard-requires storage-account shared keys — incompatible with this account's allowSharedKeyAccess:false (github.com/Azure/azure-cli/issues/32912). layer-06-platform.yml now creates the export via `az rest` against the Exports REST API (api-version 2023-08-01) requesting `identity: { type: SystemAssigned }` explicitly, then grants that identity's principalId — read back from the PUT response, never a resourceId or clientId — Storage Blob Data Contributor via an explicit `az role assignment create`, scoped to the cost-exports container (not the whole storage account). F13 remains open: cost-ingest's Storage Blob Data Reader grant is blocked on F19 (cost-ingest has no Function App or identity anywhere in this repo's IaC despite infra-up.yml:31 claiming otherwise). F13 remains this control's sole remaining open contributor, carrying forward the same gapSeverity — six of seven grants landing does not close a finding defined as 'zero workload RBAC expressed in IaC' while one still is not. CLOSED (2026-08-28, commit c33f06e -- F19, on explicit sponsor authorisation). F13's seventh and last documented grant -- cost-ingest -> Storage Blob Data Reader -- is now expressed in code. It could not be before: F19 meant apps/cost-ingest, a complete and tested Azure Functions app, appeared in no Bicep anywhere, so it had no Function App, no identity, and therefore no principal for the grant to be written against. infra/bicep/platform/main.bicep now provisions the Function App on a Flex Consumption (FC1) plan with a user-assigned identity, and grants that identity Storage Blob Data Reader (2a2b9908-6ea1-4ae2-8e65-a410df84e7d1) scoped to the cost-exports CONTAINER -- not the storage account and not the subscription -- via the new infra/bicep/platform/modules/blob-container-role.bicep. Flex Consumption is a least-privilege choice as much as a cost one: it is the only plan that supports a managed-identity AzureWebJobsStorage with no Azure Files shared-key connection string, so the Function introduces no stored credential (CLAUDE.md hard rule 5); and because that plan supports only the Event Grid-based blob trigger, the Function keeps no blob receipts or poison queue in the account it watches, which is what lets the grant there stay a pure read. The three account-wide roles the Functions host requires (Storage Blob Data Owner, Storage Queue Data Contributor, Storage Table Data Contributor) bind to a SECOND, empty runtime storage account created for that purpose, never to the cost-export account -- consolidating them would have handed the identity Owner-class blob access to the very container this grant narrows it to. Its OneLake write access is Fabric workspace Contributor (infra/fabric/provision-workspace.ps1, -CostIngestPrincipalId, wired from layer-07-apps.yml): Viewer is read-only and cannot create Files/cost_daily/, Contributor is the lowest of Fabric's four workspace roles that can write, and Fabric exposes no data-plane role narrower than the workspace -- it is the broadest grant any workload identity holds in this estate and is argued for at the grant itself. STATUS MOVES TO CLOSED because every finding this review raised against this control is now addressed -- F7 (Task 9), F8 (Task 10), F10 (Task 11) and now F13 -- and CLOSED here means exactly what compliance/README.md's Register vocabulary says it means: no known open finding stands against this control. It is not a claim that the control is met, that the estate was assessed exhaustively, or that anything was verified against a live tenant. WHAT IS AND IS NOT VERIFIED. Nothing in this estate has ever been deployed; no Azure, Entra or Fabric call was made to build or test any of this. The evidence is repo-static -- it describes what the repository DECLARES. verification/tests/cost-ingest.Tests.ps1 (43 assertions) asserts the role definition GUID and the container scope against comment-stripped Bicep, never against comment text (the F27 ruling), refuses any role GUID outside the four this leg documents, and checks that the account-wide host roles bind only to the runtime storage account; infra/fabric/tests/provision-workspace.Tests.ps1 asserts the Fabric role string per principal. Three surgical mutations were run against those suites and each turned exactly the intended assertions red: widening the container grant to account scope (1 failure), dropping the user-assigned identity (1 failure), widening the Fabric role to Member (6 failures). STILL OUTSTANDING, and carried in the recommendation below rather than dropped: F13's Fix text also called for a V7.x audit criterion asserting each principal holds exactly its expected roles and no others. That does not exist. A live-tenant criterion has never had a tenant to assert against, and the static tests above guard what this repository declares, not what any subscription holds.

recommendation: No open finding remains against this control. The deployer's Graph grant is Application.ReadWrite.OwnedBy rather than .All, mls-verifier is federated to its own environment:verify subject, the NIST policy identity holds no role assignment it cannot use, and all seven documented workload grants are expressed in least-privilege form (Tasks 9, 10, 11, 12, 17, F24 and F19). STILL OUTSTANDING: add a V7.x Verifier criterion asserting that each workload principal holds exactly its expected roles at exactly its expected scopes, and no others, read back from ARM as mls-verifier. All seven grants are now expressed in IaC and guarded by static tests over this repository, but no criterion has ever compared that declaration against a deployed tenant -- because nothing has ever been deployed.
